description:
A local-first workspace for teams of AI agents.

Autohand Squad is a local-first workspace for agent teams. It runs a local runtime, desktop controller, analytics, and release pipeline so you can work with your dream team of AI agents.
Stable release. Recommended for everyone.
Source: 21fe46b2e74c
What's new
Added
- See and delete the files a member made. A member's Library now also lists "Made in its folders": the images, documents and code it created or changed in its work folders, recorded after each reply on any engine. Move a file it created to the Trash, or delete a file it published to its Library. Files it only edited stay yours to decide.
- Marketplace admin can add and edit Autohand's agents. Admin › Squad › Marketplace on autohand.ai now adds new agents (saved unpublished until you publish), edits an Autohand agent's name, face, instructions, skills, tagline, category, tags and the connectors its page shows, and publishes or unpublishes it. Draft with AI fills the form from a short brief, Suggestions proposes agents people searched for and did not find, and Stats shows the most popular agents, categories and searches.
- Members run on your other computers, over SSH. Settings › Computers now starts with where your members run: this computer, computers Over SSH, Cloud computers and the other computers in your account. Add a Mac or Linux computer that runs Squad by user and host, with a key from your ~/.ssh or your ssh agent; Test says in one sentence whether Squad answers there. Squad keeps an encrypted SSH connection to it, so nothing is opened to the internet, and each member's Runs on offers it in one click.
- Cloud computers (Beta): New cloud computer lists Hetzner Cloud, DigitalOcean, Amazon Lightsail, Fly.io and your own server, with the steps to set one up in your own account and add it over SSH. Squad doesn't create them for you yet.
- Other computers in your account lists the computers you've connected through the relay, by name and when each last connected.
- Member profiles live in your Autohand account. When you're signed in, each member's name, role, description, instructions, personality, skills, bird and voice are kept in your account and follow you to your other computers, and to your phone through either one. Edit a member on one computer and the other picks it up within half a minute. If both changed the same thing, Settings › Cloud sync shows both and lets you keep this computer's or use your account's; nothing is overwritten unseen. Members you have on another computer are listed there with Add to this computer. Folders, permissions, model settings and memories stay on each computer. Turn it off with Keep member profiles in your Autohand account. A Squad owned by a team keeps profiles with the team only after you turn it on.
- Change a member's avatar, personality and skills from your iPhone. In Squad for iPhone, a member's Edit Profile now also picks one of Squad's 300 birds, edits the personality and chooses skills from the ones on this computer. The change is saved here, like an edit made in this window.
Changed
- Calmer, clearer loading. A member's reply in progress now shows its stage as softly shimmering words instead of a spinner, and channels show "is typing…" the same way. A member's task list marks each step with an empty circle, a turning ring or a green check. Saving memory settings says "Saving…" then "Saved" with a check, the update download shows a thin bar with its percentage, the connectors catalogue slides a thin bar while it loads, and History shows placeholder rows instead of "Loading…". With reduced motion on, nothing sweeps or slides.
- The phone's "From anywhere" is now Reach from anywhere, through Squad relay by Autohand, with the relay's address and how it's doing ("Connected · 38 ms", or when it last answered). Use a different relay points phones at a relay you or your team run; it must be an HTTPS address. The channel-sharing relay page is now called Team relay.
Fixed
- Squad no longer stops on "Your device's local storage is full" when your disk has space. That screen was about Squad's own small window cache (about 5 MB), filled by chat history, not your disk. Squad now makes room by keeping history in memory for the session (the computer already keeps the real copy) and opens normally; members are kept first.
- Your squad comes back after updating from an older Squad. Updating from a version before 0.1.22 opened setup with no members, although your squad was still on the computer. Squad now brings it back by itself the first time you open it: members, channels, chats and memories, with members paused until you look them over. A line at the top says so, with Undo. If your Squad was already set up again, or another account signs in on the same computer, the same line offers "Bring back your earlier squad" instead, with the folders filled in. Your earlier files are never changed.
